_comment: Complete schema example. The account, people, figures, and sources are fictional; copy the shape, never the content. Optional features shown here: `manual: true` on an account-team-supplied opportunity (no deal_key, no meetings, matching coverage row with 0 analyzed); `dimensions` on the strategic narrative (the five-part checklist in SKILL.md step 8); `points` on any block, which renders bullets instead of prose and is required for pptx output; `account_team` plus `account_team_note`; and `budget_cycle` with a declared `basis`.

relationship_health.text: Three open opportunities worth $441,000 across two domains, one of them supplied by the account team with no call evidence, plus $210,000 closed won in the last 24 months. Meeting cadence has held at roughly weekly since March and the most recent customer meeting was 2026-08-10. Coverage is concentrated: 26 of 34 meetings involve the Platform Engineering group, and the EU entity has appeared on 4 calls in six months.

business_priorities.title: Cut cross-border transit exceptions by a third by FY27
business_priorities.text: Named on the Q2 earnings call as the primary operating target for the EU network, owned by the COO.

challenges.title: Exception handling is manual across three systems
challenges.text: The operations team reconciles exceptions by hand between the TMS, the customs broker portal, and a spreadsheet. Two named analysts spend most of a shift on it. So what: this is the mechanism behind the COO's FY27 target, and it is the use case the expansion opportunity addresses.
challenges.evidence: We have two people whose whole job is chasing exceptions between three screens.

kpis.title: Exception rate per thousand shipments
kpis.text: The metric the operations group reports upward each month.

industry_trends.title: EU customs data requirements tighten in 2027
industry_trends.text: The new filing regime adds fields that Northwind's broker portal does not currently capture, which lands directly on the exception workflow above.
industry_trends.source: European Commission implementing regulation summary, retrieved 2026-08-22

strengths.text: Owns bonded warehouse capacity at three of the five largest EU entry points, which competitors lease.
Investment grade balance sheet with headroom for network capex, which funds multi-year platform commitments.

weaknesses.text: Systems integration debt from the 2023 acquisition is unresolved; the EU entity still runs a separate TMS.
Exception handling is manual across three systems, tying up two analysts a shift.

opportunities.text: Freight brokerage consolidation is leaving mid-market shippers without a regional provider.
The 2027 customs filing regime rewards operators who can produce clean structured data at the border.
opportunities.source: European Commission implementing regulation summary, retrieved 2026-08-22

threats.text: Two digital-native forwarders have entered the Rotterdam to Atlanta lane with published rates.
Shipper-side rate transparency tools are compressing margin on standard lanes.

hypotheses.text: Engineering groups outside Platform hold their own tooling budgets.
hypotheses.question: Ask Raman which groups outside Platform Engineering approve their own tooling spend.

priority.text: Post Sales and ADR first. The EU Rollout has had no customer attendee in 79 days against a live opportunity, which is the single point of failure in the account, and the Atlanta hub runs the evidenced use case with zero engagement, which is the largest uncovered surface. Customer Education runs earlier than its urgency suggests because it produces the quantified metric every other track is currently missing.
priority.source: CRM, meeting metadata, and MEDDPICC Metrics across 34 meetings

tracks.title: ADR Strategy
tracks.definition: Account development and outbound prospecting inside the account. Owns net new entry into business units, regions, and personas with no existing relationship.
tracks.objective: Open the Atlanta hub as a third opportunity this quarter.
tracks.why_now: Atlanta runs the same three-system exception workflow evidenced in Rotterdam (M. Devlin, 2026-06-18) and has never appeared on any of 34 meetings.
plays: Ask Devlin for an introduction to his Atlanta counterpart at the 9/3 operations review, before any cold sequence.
Reuse the Rotterdam exception narrative rather than a generic sequence, since the workflow is confirmed identical.
tracks.owner: Unassignable from the confirmed account team, which has no ADR member.
tracks.exit_criterion: A discovery call held with a named Atlanta operations owner.

tracks.title: Customer Education
tracks.definition: Enablement of the customer's own users: onboarding, training, certification, workshops, documentation, and community.
tracks.objective: Instrument the Rotterdam pilot so it produces a defensible before-and-after number.
tracks.why_now: Devlin described roughly half a shift per day saved for two analysts (2026-07-22) but no figure has been attached, and both the expansion business case and any executive conversation currently rest on that gap.
plays: Agree the exception-rate baseline with Devlin before the expansion review.
Run a working session with the two operations analysts to capture time-on-task before and after.
tracks.owner: Priya Raman by default. Education is not her role and this is a gap to fill.
tracks.exit_criterion: A customer-confirmed baseline and current figure for exceptions per thousand shipments.

tracks.title: CSE / PS Strategy
tracks.definition: Solutions engineering and professional services. Owns technical validation, integration scoping, implementation, and services attach.
tracks.objective: Close out the EU integration questions so the rollout is not gated on architecture.
tracks.why_now: Okonkwo is the sole technical contact on the EU Rollout and the separate EU TMS has not been scoped (S. Okonkwo, 2026-06-04).
plays: Scope the EU TMS integration in writing and identify whether the existing security approval covers the parent entity.
Separate blockers to the current use case from blockers to full rollout in the scoping note.
tracks.exit_criterion: A written integration scope with open items owned and dated.

tracks.title: Post Sales Strategy
tracks.definition: Customer success ownership after signature: success plan, health monitoring, QBR cadence, escalation path, and the renewal motion.
tracks.objective: Restore contact on the EU Rollout and put a success plan behind the live Rotterdam deployment.
tracks.why_now: No customer-side attendee from the EU entity since 2026-06-04, which is 79 days, on an opportunity carrying $145,000.
plays: Re-open the EU thread through Okonkwo with the 2027 customs filing change as the reason to talk.
Stand up a success plan for Rotterdam covering the exception metric, so the renewal conversation has evidence behind it.
tracks.exit_criterion: A meeting held with an EU-entity attendee, and a written success plan shared with Devlin.
needs_input: Named CSM and planned QBR cadence.
